text:
incident-bot: Paging: p99 latency spike detected for /v1/stream -> eu-west2 (streaming stalls). Autopage to oncall. Severity: SEV2. Pager: @alice

alice (oncall): saw the page, joining. any initial customer impact? :eyes:

sam (support): customer-facing symptoms: streaming clients see stalled event chunks ~15-45s, retries from SDKs. Several active customers reporting degraded UX. No wide request errors, just hangs.

ben (sre): checking traces now, p50 fine, p95 up ~600ms, p99 jumping to 9-12s for chunk tail. Looks correlated with NAT egress for eu-west2 -> cross-zone hops.

maria (eng-runtime): is this the same pattern as last month's tail-handshake noise? stack shows many sessions stuck in TLS handshake state on proxy.

jon (netops): I see elevated retransmits and SYN-RTT on the interzone path: tx drops, path switching between azb/azc. NAT ephemeral port churn is high.

alice (oncall): ok triage plan: 1) determine customer impact and scope 2) mitigate routing/nat 3) roll forward fixes or roll back recent route changes. Assigning roles: ben+jon network triage, maria runtime checks, sam+cust-success own customer comms.

sam (support): I'll patch status page: "Investigating streaming stalls in eu-west2, intermittent tail latency/handshake delays, working on mitigation". Posting a KB link to affected customers now. :writing_hand:

lisa (cust-success): I have one enterprise on standby, prepping scripted note. Want ETA before I ping them?

alice (oncall): aim for mitigation within 20m, update at +10m.

ben (sre): pulling connection state metrics... conntrack table utilization at 83% on nat-gw-1, ephemeral ports high, ephemeral reuse causing 4xx? More importantly TCP retransmit spikes coincide with crosszone route flaps.

jon (netops): running quick egress steer to alternate NAT pool (nat-gw-2) for eu-west2-streaming-route. Command: ```aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-xyz --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --nat-gateway-id nat-0123abcd``` Doing controlled swap for subset. I'll move 25% of traffic first.

maria (eng-runtime): enabling aggressive prefix-KV cache and increasing streaming keepalive to 10s to avoid reconnect storms while we reroute. Patch applied to canary instances.

incident-bot: NOTE: reroute job started by jon at 2999994380.

ben (sre): after shifting 25% to nat-gw-2 p99 dropped from ~10s to ~1.2s for that subset. Good signal. Continue ramp.

jon (netops): ramping to 100% now. Replacing routes across azb/azc, propagating. Expect 45-60s to fully converge.

alice (oncall): monitoring streaming tail metrics and client retries. maria, watch for any increase in application-level errors when keepalive change rolls.

maria (eng-runtime): saw no new 5xx, only a spike of aborted streams during the switch (~0.2% of requests). We have fallback logic on client to reconnect which is working.

sam (support): customer impact update posted. Some customers saw 1-2 reconnects. No data loss reported.

jon (netops): route swap complete at 2999994502. Conntrack utilization back down to 47% on nat-gw-2. Retransmits reduced, TLS handshake median back to ~120ms, p99 ~1.1s.

ben (sre): continuing to watch for 15m. Will also run packet captures on old path for root cause. Suspect asymmetric egress causing retransmit amplification between AZs.

alice (oncall): escalation decision: keep nat-gw-2 as active for streaming; open follow-up for durable fix. Who owns long term? jon for net config + ben for telemetry alerts + maria for runtime backoffs.

maria (eng-runtime): immediate runtime mitigations applied: keepalive bump, increased KV cache TTL to reduce new connections. We'll plan quantifiable rollout to prod after postmortem.

jon (netops): preliminary notes: observed packet loss spike ~0.6-0.9% on inter-AZ link at 2999994310-2999994450; route flapping due to BGP adj transient; ephemeral-port exhaustion exacerbated the tail for long-lived streaming connections.

ben (sre): capture snippets: ```tcpdump -nni eth0 'tcp[tcpflags] & (tcp-syn|tcp-fin) != 0' -c 2000 > /tmp/syn-capture.pcap``` saved to S3: https://artifacts.example.com/pcaps/2999994321/syn-capture.pcap

lisa (cust-success): I'll send a personalized note to affected enterprise customers summarizing: cause suspected inter-AZ packet loss & NAT churn, temporary reroute to alternate NAT pool mitigated impact; next update after postmortem.

sam (support): status page edited with mitigation details and "degraded" -> "degraded: mitigation in place".

incident-bot: Incident set to Mitigated at 2999994620 by alice. Open follow-up: #INC-2026-078: crosszone-handshake-tail-postmortem. Owner: ben. Sev: SEV2 -> P0 follow-up.

alice (oncall): Thanks team. Action items: ben collect graphs + packet captures; jon propose BGP/route stability fixes and increase conntrack headroom; maria evaluate client reconnect/backoff improvements and KV caching tradeoffs; sam/lisa prep customer followups. Update channel when postmortem doc is ready.

ben (sre): putting initial timeline & impact summary in ops-runbook: "~00:12h total customer impact window, affecting ~0.7% of streaming sessions in eu-west2, median extra latency during window ~600ms, p99 up to 12s pre-mitigation. No customer data loss."

jon (netops): I'll schedule a change to increase ephemeral port pool and fix BGP adj flaps with the cloud provider.

maria (eng-runtime): will add a small eval to Redwood Optimize to detect streaming tail regressions quicker.

alice (oncall): closing thread. Reopen if regression occurs. Good mitigation. :thumbsup:
